value.title: Blueprint 003: Copilot cache proxy
value.summary: How PRD 004 is built: a same-binary sidecar (`pij-rs cache-proxy`) that holds one account's token and rewrites the cache TTL, and a daemon spawn gate that wires a Copilot Claude seat to it only when the sidecar says it is ready.

sections.name: overview
sections.value: A new pi-free crate, `crates/cache-proxy`, carries the proxy: the request rewrite from the POC (`ttl: "1h"` on every `cache_control`, `X-Initiator: agent` on tool-result continuations), the token holder (`gh auth token --user`, in memory, refreshed only on a 401, single-flight), the readiness check (`copilot_internal/user`: endpoint plus quota), and an axum listener on 127.0.0.1:7471 that streams to the discovered endpoint with reqwest. `pij-rs cache-proxy` runs it under its own LaunchAgent, so a daemon bounce never touches it. It serves a status route that the daemon reads: at spawn, to decide proxied or plain, and on one slow loopback poll, to give the prime one notice per state change. The daemon never holds the token.

value.name: Proxy core (rewrite and pass-through)
value.responsibility: Ports the POC: sets `ttl: "1h"` on every `cache_control` block, sets `X-Initiator: agent` when the last message is a tool result, maps a `*-1m` `model` to its base id (Copilot's API rejects `-1m` with 400 `model_not_supported`; the base id serves 1M), and otherwise streams requests and responses through unchanged (SSE, tool use, images, 1M context). Binds 127.0.0.1 only. Logs the upstream host, status, model (`base (from x-1m)`) and cache usage counts, never a header value.

value.name: Token holder
value.responsibility: Fetches the account's token with `gh auth token --user <account>`, with `gh` resolved once to an absolute path and recorded through `pij_core::spawns::record("gh.cache_proxy_token")`. Keeps it in memory only. On a 401, one single-flight refresh shared by every waiting request, then one retry. A failed refresh keeps the current token and raises one state change. A test-only stale-token knob (`PIJ_CACHE_PROXY_TEST_STALE_TOKEN`) serves rows 9 and 10.

value.name: Readiness check
value.responsibility: GETs `api.github.com/copilot_internal/user` with the token: takes `endpoints.api` as the upstream, and `quota_snapshots.premium_interactions` as the quota (usable if `unlimited`, `remaining > 0` or `overage_permitted`; otherwise the reset date). GETs `<endpoints.api>/models` for each Claude model's `max_prompt_tokens`. Both are cached per account for 10 minutes, and re-run after a refresh or a 402. A 402 from upstream marks the quota exhausted at once.

value.name: Status route
value.responsibility: `GET /__pij/status` on the proxy's port returns `{ready, state, reason, fix, account, upstream_host, quota: {usable, reset}, models: {"<base id>": {max_prompt_tokens}}, counters: {requests, refreshes, gh_launches, upstream_401, upstream_402}, pid, since}`. `models` lists only Claude ids, keyed by base id (never `-1m`). `state` is one of `ready`, `off`, `no_account`, `gh_missing`, `no_token`, `quota_exhausted`, `upstream_unreachable`. `POST /__pij/reload` re-reads the config file and refetches the token if the account changed. It carries no token and no secret.

value.name: pij-rs cache-proxy
value.where: crates/cli/src/cache_proxy.rs (Command::CacheProxy in crates/cli/src/main.rs, an early long-running branch beside Command::Daemon)
value.responsibility: `pij-rs cache-proxy` (no action) runs the sidecar. `status` prints the status route (or 'not listening' plus the fix). `account <login>` and `off` / `on` write the config file, then POST reload. The second-human-account check (`/usr/bin/dscl . -list /Users UniqueID`, uid 501 and up, minus `nobody`-style system ids) lives here as a pure parser plus one launch, called by `status` and doctor.

value.name: Cache-proxy config
value.responsibility: `account = "<login>"` and `enabled = true|false`. No file, or no account, means off. Written only by `pij-rs cache-proxy account|off|on`; read by the sidecar at start and on reload.

value.name: Sidecar LaunchAgent
value.where: justfile recipes `cache-proxy-autostart` / `cache-proxy-autostart-off` (plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.pij.cache-proxy.plist); `just install` calls the first
value.responsibility: Same shape as `rs-autostart`: `/bin/sh -c 'exec <npm-prefix>/bin/pij-rs cache-proxy'`, RunAtLoad plus KeepAlive (restart on crash, ThrottleInterval 10 s), so the sidecar outlives every daemon bounce.

value.name: Spawn gate and env
value.where: crates/daemon/src/cache_proxy.rs (called from launch_seat_locked in crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs); env added in build_spawn_plan, crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs
value.responsibility: For a Copilot seat only: plain if `--no-cache-proxy`, if the model isn't Claude, if the status route isn't `ready` (one loopback GET, 1 s timeout), or if the model's base id (with `-1m` stripped) is missing from the status `models`. Otherwise `SpawnPlanInput` carries the proxy URL, base id and limit, and `build_spawn_plan` adds `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7471`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID=<base id>`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS=<max_prompt_tokens>` and `COPILOT_PROVIDER_VISION=true`. Copilot CLI treats every BYOK model as text-only without `VISION` and drops images (s02 row 16; every Claude id in `/models` has vision). `MODEL_ID` sets only limits and agent config; the wire model is the seat's `--model`, which the proxy maps from `-1m`. OMP, Claude and Codex seats are never touched.

value.name: Seat proxy state and receipt
value.where: SeatDescriptor (crates/core) field `cache_proxy: {state: proxied|plain, reason}`; SpawnResponse in crates/daemon/src/http/types.rs; directory holder rows (crates/daemon/src/community/directory.rs, rendered in crates/cli/src/main.rs render_directory)
value.responsibility: Every Copilot spawn records proxied or plain with the reason and fix; the spawn receipt prints it; directory rows show it. A seat with no field (launched before the proxy existed) reads as plain.

value.name: Proxy watch and notices
value.responsibility: Reads the status route every 30 s (one loopback GET, no launch). On a change of `state` (or on unreachable), it sends one notice per change to each prime through `notify_prime` (crates/daemon/src/http/routes.rs), naming the proxied live seats and the fix, never repeats. Exposes the last status and counters in `/health`, so `pij-rs --json ping` and `just doctor` show them.

value.name: Doctor row
value.responsibility: Adds `cache-proxy:` with `pij-rs cache-proxy status` (state, account, upstream host, quota, counters, proxied and plain live seats), and the second-human-account warning.

value.decision: A same-binary sidecar with its own LaunchAgent and port, not a task inside the daemon.
value.why: Prime ruling 5 (2026-11-18): a bounce closes the daemon's listener for only ~567 ms, but it cuts in-flight streams that run for minutes, and the daemon bounces several times a day. Same binary: no new artifact, and the Defender exclusion for ~/.local/share/pij/bin/pij-rs already covers it.

value.decision: The token lives only in the sidecar. The daemon reads the status route and never sees the token.
value.why: One holder means one place to audit (security verdict), and the daemon's logs and env, which reach every job it runs, can't leak it.

value.decision: Refresh only on a 401, single-flight, one retry. No proactive refresh.
value.why: Spike q-01: the `gho_` token is accepted directly, sends no expiration header, and the v2/token exchange returns 403.

value.decision: The quota check is `copilot_internal/user` `quota_snapshots`, not a model probe.
value.why: Spike: `/models` answers 200 with the quota exhausted, `/v1/messages` gives 402; `copilot_internal/user` shows `remaining 0, overage_permitted false` plus the reset date, for a free GET. Prime accepted 2026-11-18.

value.decision: A feature-specific config file (`~/.pij-rs/cache-proxy.toml`) set by `pij-rs cache-proxy account|off|on`, not a generic `pij config` store.
value.why: pij has no generic config store (its config is per feature, such as peers.toml); building one for two keys is scope the PRD doesn't ask for. Answers PRD q-03.

value.decision: The gate's last word is the sidecar's own `ready`, read at spawn with a 1 s timeout; any failure means plain.
value.why: The sidecar is the only part that knows the token, the endpoint and the quota. A plain launch is always safe; a broken proxied seat never is.

value.decision: Proxy-death detection is a 30 s loopback poll from the daemon, not a push from the sidecar.
value.why: A dead sidecar can't push. One GET per 30 s, with no launch and no growth with seats, is the cheapest signal that also catches a hang.

value.rate: 0 launches per request; one upstream HTTPS request per seat request (the same request the seat would send directly)
value.scaling: with seat requests; adds no process

value.rate: 1 `gh` launch (absolute path) per sidecar start, plus at most 1 per 401 burst (single-flight); 0 per request
value.scaling: with sidecar restarts and 401 bursts, not with seats

value.rate: 1 GET to `copilot_internal/user` and 1 to `/models` per 10 min per account while asked, plus 1 of each after a refresh or 402; 0 launches
1 loopback GET per Copilot spawn; 0 launches

value.scaling: constant: not per seat, not per pane

value.rate: 1 `/usr/bin/dscl` launch per `cache-proxy status` or doctor run; never on a timer

value.change: First draft, after the step 1 spike (takin) and the prime's ruling 5 (sidecar).
req-13 (takin's spike addendum): c-proxy-core maps `-1m` to the base id; c-readiness reads `/models`; the status route gains `models`; c-spawn-gate sets the model id and max prompt tokens.
